zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## Waller為聯準會暫停升息留空間，美債上漲

Christopher Waller表示，若通膨持續改善，聯準會9月可以維持利率不變，帶動美債上漲。交換市場反映的升息25個基點機率，從本週稍早約70%降至50%附近。2年期殖利率下降5個基點至4.34%，10年與30年期各降2個基點至4.77%及5.25%；2s10s與2s30s均擴大3個基點，分別為43及91個基點。

他的談話讓市場重新考慮是否有必要緊縮，卻不必以經濟轉弱為前提。ISM服務業指數升至55.4，新訂單為2023年2月以來最高，投入價格也加速，只有聘僱仍疲弱。10年期實質殖利率下降3個基點至2.42%，損益兩平通膨率卻升1個基點至2.35%。WTI與布蘭特收$91.79及$95.91，週漲幅仍接近10%與7%。

股市歡迎聯準會可能保留耐心。S&P 500上漲1.06%、Nasdaq 100漲1.16%，VIX降至14.32。美元指數下跌0.59%至5月以來最低，黃金期貨大漲3.65%至$4,525.70。美國投資級與高收益利差近乎不變，強勢貨幣新興市場債利差小幅收窄。巴基斯坦完成創紀錄美元發債，ByteDance擴大銀行借款，Cerba則進入法院監督的債務協商。

這次漲勢只收復部分前期跌幅。2年與5年期殖利率一週仍上升14個基點，10年期升10個基點，30年期升6個基點。Waller也將眼前決策與美債長期壓力分開：財政赤字、AI投資的資金需求，以及美債安全資產溢價減弱，都使他上調中性利率估計。9月不升息，並不會消除長債面對的這些壓力。

## 服務業訂單強，Waller等待的是通膨改善而非衰退

即使7月PCE通膨達3.7%，Waller仍認為政策僅略具限制性。他預期接下來消費者與生產者物價數據應屬合理，因為能源成本尚未廣泛擴散，也擔心在通膨開始下降時反而升息。若持續朝2%前進，可以維持3.50%至3.75%的政策區間；若再加速，則可能需要升息。他沒有提出數值門檻，並表示即使只是小幅加速，也可能改變判斷。

委員會尚未形成共識。7月有三名官員主張升息25個基點，Kevin Warsh在Jackson Hole的談話也曾強化市場的升息預期。Waller發言後，年底前預期緊縮幅度由最高41個基點降至34個基點。他願意等待，代表決策中多了一個有影響力的聲音，不是全體已同意按兵不動。

8月服務業數據顯示，需求尚不足以讓聯準會放心。ISM由54.1升至55.4，高於約54.2的預估，為六個月最強。新訂單增加3.7點至60.9，價格支付增加2.3點至72.6；供應商交貨由52.8降至51.3，但已連續21個月高於50。S&P Global服務業PMI終值由54.6升至56.5，略低於56.8初值。

聘僱是相對疲弱的一環，ISM就業指數仍在47.8的收縮區。8月29日止當週初領增加2,000至20.6萬，前週上修為20.4萬，四週平均20.725萬。續領增加8,000至177.9萬，四週平均卻減少5,000至178.175萬。聘僱偏弱，但尚未出現裁員急增。

7月貿易逆差可能拖累GDP，細項卻仍反映強勁投資。逆差較上月擴大24.4%，由修正後$712億升至$886億。出口減少$66億、2.1%至$3,107億；進口增加$108億、2.8%至$3,993億。商品逆差$1,196億，服務順差$310億。資本財進口增加$144億，其中電腦增$69億、配件增$66億，與持續的科技投資相符，不能單純解讀為最終需求疲弱。

Waller認為，資金競爭、財政疑慮，以及美債安全性與流動性溢價下降，都支持更高的中性利率。他指出聯邦債務接近$40兆，2026財政年度赤字約GDP 6%；若結構性赤字不能大幅趨近於零，單靠成長很難明顯降低債務負擔。他也不預期長債買回規模加倍能持久壓低殖利率，本月將進行首次至少$40億操作。改善舊券流動性，本身不會改變政府融資需求。

交易增幅集中於對政策較敏感的天期。名目附息債以原始面額計算的成交量增加6.1%至$8,657億；2年以內增加31.1%至$2,017億，超過3年至5年增加16.4%至$2,432億。這反映重新定價時交易活絡，並不是淨買入金額。

## 日圓漲勢獲日本央行訊號支持，未見再次大舉干預的證據

日圓上漲2%至每美元155.52，市場對日本央行9月的行動也更明確。報導指出，官員傾向從目前1%升息25個基點，認為經濟變化尚不足以支持50個基點，但若通膨上行風險持續，後續步調仍可調整。交換市場幾乎完全反映首次升息，12月再升機率約80%；空頭回補與本地避險擴大匯率反應。

央行帳戶資料不支持又一次大規模干預。日本央行預估財政因素將使往來帳戶減少¥4,100億，貨幣經紀商估計約¥7,000億，差額低於2022年以來最小一次干預的¥7,290億。相較先前¥15.4兆干預，這次資料顯示，最新日圓漲勢主要來自政策與部位調整，而非再次大舉官方買入。

財務大臣片山皋月表示，政府對匯率仍保持同樣急迫感，也反映首相高市早苗的立場，但否認Scott Bessent在會面中提出絕對要求。高田先前不排除較大幅度或連續升息；最新官員說法則將9月較可能的步幅縮至25個基點，未排除之後加快。

日本30年期標售在4%以上吸引買盤。投標倍數3.79低於前次3.86，仍高於12個月平均3.52。公布結果前，殖利率一度下降10個基點至4.065%，期貨之後保住漲幅。不過，平均與最低得標價格之差由0.21擴大至0.28，顯示面對政府支出計畫及進一步政策正常化，買方仍要求一定讓利。

GPIF管理委員會8月21日開會，是七年來首次公開宣布8月會議，距離上次認為不需檢討配置僅五個月。這提供重新考慮的跡象，還不是已更改投資比重。規模¥318兆的基金，仍以本國與外國債券、股票各25%為目標。10年期日債殖利率自3月升約1個百分點、一度突破3%，使本地債券更具吸引力。

海外債券投資人也可能不賣債，只增加匯率避險。6月底，日本、加拿大、台灣等六個市場的外幣曝險避險比率為41%，至少2015年以來最低；以調查涵蓋的$4.6兆曝險計算，比例增加5個百分點就代表約$2,300億交易。日圓投資人三個月美元避險成本，已從2023年10月6%降至2.75%；日本投資人上半年新買外債的避險比率41%，低於2024年62%。利差縮小若促使避險增加，可能壓低美元，未必伴隨美債出售。

## 歐洲能源缺口讓下一次升息仍難避免

歐洲還需注入逾100太瓦時天然氣，按目前價格約€70億以上，才能達到歐盟最低75%儲氣目標。所需的季末注氣速度，2022年能源危機後未再出現。天然氣在三日上漲10%後暫穩，但冷冬、中國搶購、管線中斷或美國LNG供應受阻，都會增加冬季風險。

調查的65名經濟學家全數預期歐洲央行將升息25個基點至2.50%，高於8月83%的比例。與市場的分歧在之後：91%預期年底維持2.50%，78%預期到2027年中仍如此，期貨卻反映再升一次。8月服務業PMI由51.7小降至51.6，綜合指數維持52.0；製造業抵銷海外服務需求減少，使整體出口訂單四年半來首次增加。服務業聘僱為八個月最強，帶來2026年首次民間淨增聘。服務投入成本及收費均達三個月高點，綜合產出價格降溫也停頓，整體通膨仍為3.3%。

英國央行首席經濟學家Huw Pill主張，及早升息可避免暫時性通膨變得持久，也能減少日後更激烈緊縮的需要。他是7月三名主張升息的委員之一，態度比市場定價更積極：期貨反映9月升息機率略高於15%，11月則逾70%。

高殖利率已吸引英國家庭回流。Freetrade週二債券交易筆數與金額均為今年最高，Hargreaves Lansdown則創5月15日以來最活絡的英債買盤。2056年到期、票息5.375%的債券，以及2028年與2061年到期的低票息券都受關注；當時10年殖利率接近5.2%、30年近5.8%。重視稅務效益的零售買方提供部分需求，但持有量仍不到流通債券4%。

馬來西亞如22名經濟學家中20人預期，維持2.75%，卻刪去2025年9月以來一直使用的政策「適當」措辭。交換市場未來12個月緊縮幅度增加14個基點，累計升息50個基點的機率接近50%，原先則大致只反映25個基點。今年約5%的成長、包括第2季6%，使央行有空間因應7月1.8%通膨可能加速。

土耳其通膨則由31.8%降至31.5%，低於31.6%預估。月增1.84%也低於1.92%預期，雖高於前月1.78%。2年期里拉債殖利率降14個基點至39.6%。融資利率由實際40%回到政策37%，使降息較有可能；核心通膨、能源與預期惡化，卻仍要求謹慎。

波蘭官員Iwona Duda預期3.75%利率將維持至年底，反對降息，也不認為需立即升息；遠期市場卻反映12個月約三次、每次25個基點。通膨3.4%為14個月高點，接近2.5%目標容許區間的上緣，燃料限價到期與肥料成本可能使其超出範圍。

匈牙利據報準備在連降三次、每次25個基點後暫停於5.5%，並將通膨目標從3%降至2.5%。符合政府朝歐元接軌的方向，帶動福林對歐元最多升1.5%、債券殖利率下降。7月通膨1.2%讓目標調整不必立即伴隨緊縮；但預計GDP 7.5%的赤字，以及惠譽對可信債務路徑的要求，使財政執行更困難。

澳洲則顯示，強健主權評等難以隔絕全球長債壓力。截至週三的一個月，10年殖利率升約30個基點至5.25%，創15年高點，漲幅超過同業，儘管三大機構均評AAA、公共債務也低於美英。3月外資持有比率51%，高於一年前46%。避險後主權債指數今年仍回報0.3%，對照美債及全球政府債分別虧損0.7%與0.6%。

## 巴基斯坦創紀錄籌美元，印度考慮回收過剩流動性

巴基斯坦募集創紀錄$30億：5年期$17.5億、殖利率7.75%，10年期$12.5億、8.25%。訂單接近$60億，行銷期間利差收窄約25個基點，最終殖利率與同級借款人相近。穆迪B3仍低於投資級六個級距，但評等上調、IMF計畫及全球高收益溢價接近數十年低點，支持融資；2031年債小升至99.65美分。

面對約$220億外部融資需求，資金將用於償還昂貴短債、延長到期。阿聯在連續七年展延後，拒絕再續作$30億，需由沙烏地阿拉伯提供替代支持。巴基斯坦另尋求中國$13億商業貸款再融資；中國是最大債權人，餘額逾$250億。三年策略也考慮伊斯蘭債與人民幣債。這次發行降低部分雙邊資金續作依賴，仍未涵蓋全部需求。

印度眼前的問題卻是吸收超預期外幣。優惠計畫募集創紀錄$1,270億FCNR存款，加上相關貸款逾$1,360億，原先目標至少$800億。計畫提前一個月於8月31日結束。與央行直接交換支持盧比、降低銀行資金成本，卻使體系流動性達創紀錄₹9.7兆、約$1,026.6億。

銀行主管如今提議用美元兌盧比賣出後買回交換，而非提高現金準備率。至多一年的天期，可配合央行估計一年內到期的約$450億美元遠期空頭，在展延外匯曝險時回收盧比。售債與提高準備率仍是選項；銀行反對後者，因為會壓縮利差收入。

菲律賓披索創低、油價上升，使國庫重新考慮9月₱3,800億融資計畫中的5年期大型發行。7月通膨已連三個月放慢，仍達6.2%，超過年度目標兩倍。9月逾₱1,000億零售債、10月另₱500億到期，即使成本提高也難輕易取消。最新5年期標售投標倍數僅1.2，低於前次可比標售3.1。

委內瑞拉2027年債升至54美分、接近四個月高點，投資人因先前公布的美國石油協議而調整回收估值。連同未付利息，目前價格仍不到債權三分之一。分析師認為產量一至兩年內可能達每日150萬桶；一項估計將PDVSA商業債務與本幣義務都納入後，總債權可達$2,290億，政治轉型情境減記26%、延續現狀則83%。價格先上漲，債權範圍、債務可持續性及實際投資仍未談定。

IMF總裁Kristalina Georgieva警告，已開發國家殖利率、能源通膨及AI資金競爭，可能逆轉較窮國家近期債務可持續性的改善。她仍認為市場有序，並特別將塞內加爾視為加快G20共同框架處理的測試。

## 發債再挑戰紀錄，個別借款人的限制逐漸顯現

交易商估計9月美國投資級發債約$2,150億，高於去年$2,075億的單月紀錄，各家預估介於$1,900億至$2,500億。今年前八個月已有四個月創各該月份紀錄，包括最近三個月。殖利率逾5.5%並未關閉市場：本週多數時間利差低於80個基點，促使企業提前籌措2027年資金。

AI大型交易接連出現，也帶來集中度問題。許多投資級委託對單一企業設3%至5%上限；大型科技借款人即使尚未觸及，更多發行仍讓買方能比較每筆新增曝險的替代選擇。

ByteDance在銀行承諾強勁後，將原先$200億目標擴至$296億美元貸款並完成融資，為亞洲2026年第二大美元借款，用於加速AI投資。Public Storage則討論首次加幣發債，約C$5億、七年期，初步指引為政府債加95個基點左右，接續先前以C$12億收購68處設施。其美國優先無擔保評等為A2/A。

AirAsia表示，至多$10億國際債務與RM7億本地額度，將用於再融資昂貴疫情借款，而非填補營運虧損。公司4月曾發行以航線收入支持的$2.3億私人信用債，2024年另向Ares等基金借$4.43億、最高票息11%。燃油未避險、票價又難完全轉嫁，使季度虧損達RM5.27億，四年最大；伊朗戰爭以來股價下跌64%，增加降低利息負擔的融資難度。

EQT旗下Cerba Healthcare為約€50億債務申請法國協調程序。淨債務逾€49億、相當於過去一年獲利九倍，6月現金僅€1.08億。股東€1億貸款支撐流動性，貸款人將付息寬限延至11月。第2季EBITDA雖增約12%至逾€1.22億、收入增2%至€4.69億，仍不足以修復槓桿，法國醫療給付費率也不明朗。

CSN則因管理層更替而上漲。Benjamin Steinbruch掌舵逾20年後立即辭去執行長、轉任董事長，由前Vale主管Fabio Schvartsman負責營運。公司希望出售水泥與基礎設施持股募集約$29億。11%票息、2030年債上漲2.25美分至80.5，股價最多漲20%；反映出售執行信心改善，還不是已完成減債。

紐約MTA披露$7.85億發債，以成交價至少$200萬的不動產交易稅支持。今年稅收預估近$4億，2027至2030每年約$3.5億，對比新券發行後年度債務支出約$1.5億。穆迪評A1，標普最近升至AA-。本次將用滿這類證券每年本息的法定上限，償付依靠專用稅收，而非整體運輸營運。

芝加哥一般營運基金前景較弱。市長Brandon Johnson預估2027年赤字$8.82億，債券支付、生活成本調整、商品通膨與稅收增額融資剩餘款減少，都增加壓力。今年在出售欠款追收權等收入措施不如預期後，仍有$8,500萬缺口，明年另計畫補繳退休金$3.64億。再融資節省與疫情剩餘準備金處理眼前短差，未解決2027年經常收支失衡。

中國評等改革可能拉開發行人的差異。超過6,500家信用債發行人中近90%為AA以上，美國僅4.4%。標普指出，全球B級借款人的熊貓債可能被評AAA，並引用全球B類別五年累計潛在違約率15.34%。人民銀行4月起要求降低高評等集中，已促使CN¥37兆市場出現降評與撤評。

## 先看非農，接著迎來通膨與密集發債

9月4日紐約上午8:30公布非農，預估增加5.6萬，前期減2.3萬；失業率4.1%，平均時薪月增0.3%、前期0.1%。聘僱與工資偏弱可支持Waller等待，若反而強勁，則強化服務業呈現的需求訊號。

他重視的價格證據在下週：9月10日整體及核心PPI都預估月增0.3%，11日公布8月CPI。美國公債3年、10年與30年標售，以及企業恢復大量發債，將在通膨尚未明朗時爭取買盤。即使就業放慢，非能源價格僵固或投標弱，仍可能限制長債漲幅。

市場普遍預期歐洲央行9月10日升息25個基點至2.50%；經濟學家多認為升息到此為止，交易定價卻反映還有下一次，後續指引將檢驗兩者。日本央行9月18日升息25個基點已幾乎完全反映，因此後續步調更重要；若延後，或指引排除繼續升息，都會削弱日圓漲勢的政策支持，可能再次引發干預疑慮。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Waller opens the door to a Fed hold, lifting Treasuries

Treasuries rallied after Christopher Waller said further inflation progress could allow the Federal Reserve to leave rates unchanged in September. Swaps put the chance of a quarter-point increase near 50%, down from about 70% earlier in the week. The 2-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.34%, while the 10- and 30-year declined 2 basis points to 4.77% and 5.25%. Both 2s10s and 2s30s steepened 3 basis points, to 43 and 91.

Waller's comments gave investors room to reconsider tightening without requiring a weaker growth outlook. ISM services rose to 55.4, with new orders at their highest since February 2023 and input prices accelerating. Hiring remained soft. Ten-year real yields fell 3 basis points to 2.42%, but breakevens rose 1 to 2.35%; oil remained expensive, with WTI at $91.79 and Brent at $95.91, almost 10% and 7% higher over the week.

Stocks welcomed the prospect of patience. The S&P 500 gained 1.06%, Nasdaq 100 1.16% and VIX fell to 14.32. The dollar index lost 0.59% to its lowest since May, and gold futures surged 3.65% to $4,525.70. US investment-grade and high-yield spreads barely changed; hard-currency EM tightened modestly. Pakistan completed a record dollar sale and ByteDance enlarged a bank loan, even as Cerba entered court-supervised debt talks.

The rally recovered only part of the preceding selloff. Two- and 5-year yields were still 14 basis points higher over the week, the 10-year up 10 and the 30-year up 6. Waller himself distinguished the next Fed decision from longer-term pressure on Treasuries: fiscal deficits, AI demand for capital and a diminished safety premium have led him to raise his estimate of the neutral rate. A September hold would not remove those sources of pressure on long bonds.

## Strong service orders leave Waller waiting for inflation, not recession

Waller described policy as slightly restrictive despite July PCE inflation of 3.7%. He expects reasonable upcoming consumer- and producer-price readings because energy costs have not spread broadly into other prices, and sees a risk in tightening just as inflation falls. Continued progress toward 2% could justify keeping the 3.50%–3.75% funds range; renewed acceleration could warrant an increase. He offered no numerical threshold and said even a small acceleration might change his view.

The committee remains divided. Three policymakers preferred a 25-basis-point increase in July, while Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole comments had encouraged expectations of a hike. After Waller spoke, expected tightening through year-end fell to 34 basis points from as much as 41. His willingness to wait added an influential voice, not an agreed committee position.

August services data offered little reason to expect demand to do the Fed's work. ISM rose to 55.4 from 54.1, above estimates near 54.2 and the strongest in six months. New orders gained 3.7 points to 60.9; prices paid increased 2.3 to 72.6. Supplier deliveries eased to 51.3 from 52.8 but stayed above 50 for a 21st month. S&P Global's final services PMI rose to 56.5 from 54.6, slightly below its 56.8 preliminary reading.

Hiring was the weaker part of the picture. ISM employment remained in contraction at 47.8. Initial claims rose 2,000 to 206,000 in the week ended August 29, with the previous week revised to 204,000 and the four-week average at 207,250. Continuing claims increased 8,000 to 1.779 million, though their four-week average fell 5,000 to 1.78175 million. The figures suggest subdued hiring without a sharp rise in layoffs.

July trade figures also showed investment strength beneath a likely drag on GDP. The deficit widened 24.4% to $88.6 billion from a revised $71.2 billion. Exports fell $6.6 billion, or 2.1%, to $310.7 billion; imports rose $10.8 billion, or 2.8%, to $399.3 billion. The goods gap reached $119.6 billion against a $31 billion services surplus. Capital-goods imports jumped $14.4 billion, including $6.9 billion of computers and $6.6 billion of accessories, consistent with sustained technology investment rather than simply weak final demand.

Waller sees that competition for capital, fiscal concerns and erosion of Treasuries' safety and liquidity premium as reasons for a higher neutral rate. He put federal debt near $40 trillion and the fiscal 2026 deficit around 6% of GDP, arguing that growth would not substantially lower the burden without structural deficits much closer to zero. He also expected little lasting yield relief from doubling long-dated Treasury buybacks, whose first operation of at least $4 billion is due this month. Liquidity support for older securities cannot by itself change the government's financing needs.

Trading expanded most in policy-sensitive maturities. Nominal-coupon turnover rose 6.1% to $865.7 billion in original-face value. Securities maturing within 2 years traded $201.7 billion, up 31.1%, while the greater-than-3-year through 5-year sector rose 16.4% to $243.2 billion. That increase measures activity around the repricing, not net buying.

## BOJ signals, rather than another intervention, sustain the yen rally

The yen rose 2% to 155.52 per dollar as reports clarified the BOJ's likely September move. Officials favored 25 basis points from the current 1% and saw no economic change sufficient to require 50, while leaving later increases flexible if inflation risks persisted. Swaps nearly fully priced the first move and assigned about 80% odds to another in December. Short covering and domestic hedging amplified the response.

Account data argued against another large intervention. The BOJ projected a ¥410 billion fiscal drain from current accounts, versus money brokers' estimate near ¥700 billion. The difference was smaller than ¥729 billion, the smallest intervention since 2022. Following the previous ¥15.4 trillion campaign, this provided evidence that the latest rally largely reflected policy and positioning, rather than a fresh official yen purchase.

Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said the government's urgency on the currency was unchanged and reflected Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's view, but denied that Scott Bessent had made an absolute demand at their meeting. After Hajime Takata's earlier openness to larger or consecutive increases, the new BOJ account narrowed the likely September step without ruling out faster follow-through.

Japan's 30-year auction attracted demand at yields above 4%. Coverage of 3.79 was below the previous 3.86 but above the 12-month average of 3.52. The yield had fallen as much as 10 basis points to 4.065% before the result, and futures kept their gains. The tail nevertheless widened to 0.28 from 0.21: the larger gap between average and lowest accepted prices showed buyers still required some concession amid spending plans and further normalization.

GPIF's management committee met on August 21, its first publicly announced August meeting in seven years, only five months after deciding no portfolio review was needed. That is a new sign of reconsideration, not a changed allocation. The ¥318 trillion fund still targets 25% each in domestic and foreign bonds and equities. Ten-year JGB yields have risen about 1 percentage point since March and briefly exceeded 3%, making domestic bonds more competitive.

Foreign-bond investors may also adjust hedges without selling the bonds. Across six markets including Japan, Canada and Taiwan, investors hedged 41% of foreign-currency exposure at June 30, the lowest since at least 2015. A 5-percentage-point increase would mean about $230 billion of transactions against the surveyed $4.6 trillion exposure. Three-month dollar hedge costs for yen investors have fallen to 2.75% from 6% in October 2023, while Japanese investors hedged 41% of new foreign-bond purchases in the first half, versus 62% in 2024. Further hedging could weigh on the dollar as rate differentials narrow; it need not entail Treasury liquidation.

## Europe's energy shortage keeps the next hike in view

Europe needs more than 100 terawatt-hours of gas, worth over €7 billion at current prices, just to reach the EU's lowest 75% storage target. Reaching it requires a late-season injection pace not seen since the 2022 crisis. Prices steadied after a 10% rise in three days, leaving winter supplies vulnerable to cold weather, Chinese buying, pipeline outages and US LNG disruptions.

All 65 economists in a poll expected the ECB to raise its deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.50%, compared with 83% in August. The disagreement with markets comes afterward: 91% expected that rate at year-end and 78% through mid-2027, while futures priced another increase. August services PMI edged to 51.6 from 51.7 and the composite held at 52.0. Aggregate export orders rose for the first time in four and a half years as manufacturing offset weaker overseas services business. Services hiring was strongest in eight months, producing the first net private-sector job creation of 2026. Service input costs and charges reached three-month highs, and composite output-price disinflation stalled alongside 3.3% headline inflation.

BOE Chief Economist Huw Pill argued that an early increase could prevent temporary inflation becoming persistent and avoid more aggressive action later. One of July's three dissenters for a hike, he remains ahead of market timing: futures put September odds just above 15%, versus more than 70% by November.

High gilt yields are drawing households back. Freetrade recorded its busiest bond day of 2026 by number and value on Tuesday; Hargreaves Lansdown its busiest gilt day since May 15. A 5.375% issue due 2056 and low-coupon 2028 and 2061 bonds were active as 10-year yields approached 5.2% and 30-year 5.8%. Tax-sensitive demand helps at the margin, although retail ownership remains below 4% of outstanding bonds.

Malaysia held 2.75%, as 20 of 22 economists expected, but dropped the description of policy as “appropriate” used since September 2025. Swaps added 14 basis points of tightening over 12 months and approached a 50% probability of 50 basis points cumulatively, from pricing roughly one 25-basis-point move. Growth around 5% this year, including 6% in the second quarter, gives the bank room to respond if July's 1.8% inflation accelerates.

Turkey's inflation instead eased to 31.5% from 31.8%, below the 31.6% forecast. Monthly growth of 1.84% also missed the 1.92% estimate, though it rose from 1.78%. Two-year lira yields fell 14 basis points to 39.6%. With funding back at the 37% policy rate from an effective 40%, cuts look more plausible, but core inflation, energy and deteriorating expectations still argue for caution.

Poland's Iwona Duda expected the 3.75% rate to hold through 2026, rejecting cuts while seeing no immediate need to hike. Forwards priced roughly three quarter-point increases over 12 months. Inflation of 3.4%, a 14-month high, is near the upper tolerance limit around the 2.5% target; expiring fuel caps and fertilizer costs could push it beyond.

Hungary was reportedly preparing to pause at 5.5% after three 25-basis-point cuts and lower its inflation target to 2.5% from 3%. The forint gained as much as 1.5% against the euro and bond yields fell on support for the government's euro-convergence agenda. July inflation of 1.2% permits the target change without immediate tightening; a projected 7.5%-of-GDP deficit and Fitch's demand for a credible debt path make fiscal execution harder.

Australia's selloff shows how little insulation strong sovereign ratings provide from global duration pressure. Ten-year yields rose about 30 basis points over the month through Wednesday to a 15-year high of 5.25%, outpacing peers despite three triple-A ratings and lower public debt than the US and UK. Foreign ownership reached 51% in March from 46% a year earlier. The hedged sovereign index still gained 0.3% this year, against Treasury and global-government losses of 0.7% and 0.6%.

## Pakistan raises record dollars; India weighs how to absorb its surplus

Pakistan raised a record $3 billion: $1.75 billion of 5-year bonds at 7.75% and $1.25 billion of 10-year debt at 8.25%. Orders approached $6 billion and spreads tightened about 25 basis points in marketing, leaving yields broadly comparable with similarly rated borrowers. Moody's B3 rating remains six steps below investment grade, but upgrades, an IMF program and near-multidecade-low global high-yield premiums supported access. The 2031 note edged to 99.65 cents.

Proceeds will replace expensive short-term debt and extend maturities against roughly $22 billion of external financing needs. The UAE declined to roll $3 billion after seven years of renewals, requiring Saudi replacement support. Pakistan also sought refinancing of a $1.3 billion Chinese commercial loan; China is its largest creditor, with more than $25 billion outstanding. Sukuk and yuan bonds are under consideration within a three-year strategy. The sale reduces some bilateral rollover dependence without covering the whole funding requirement.

India's immediate problem is absorbing more foreign currency than expected. The incentive program attracted a record $127 billion of FCNR deposits and more than $136 billion including related loans, versus an initial ambition of at least $80 billion. It ended August 31, a month early. Direct RBI swaps helped the rupee and banks' funding costs but pushed system liquidity to a record ₹9.7 trillion, about $102.66 billion.

Bank executives now propose dollar-rupee sell-buy swaps rather than a higher cash-reserve ratio. Maturities up to one year could match roughly $45 billion of RBI short-dollar forwards estimated to mature in that period, absorbing rupees while rolling FX exposure. Bond sales and higher reserve requirements remain alternatives; banks oppose the latter because of the margin cost.

The Philippines is reconsidering a jumbo 5-year issue within September's ₱380 billion borrowing plan after the peso hit a record low and oil costs rose. July inflation had slowed for three months but remained 6.2%, more than twice the annual target. Over ₱100 billion of retail bonds mature this month and ₱50 billion in October, making cancellation difficult despite higher financing costs. The latest 5-year auction drew coverage of only 1.2, down from 3.1 at the previous comparable sale.

Venezuela's 2027 bonds rose to 54 cents, near a four-month high, as investors revised recovery estimates following the previously announced US oil agreement. Including unpaid interest, prices still imply less than one-third of claims. Analysts see output potentially reaching 1.5 million barrels a day within one or two years. One estimate puts claims as high as $229 billion if PDVSA commercial debt and local-currency obligations are included, with haircuts from 26% under a political transition to 83% under continuity. The rally precedes agreement on creditor scope, debt sustainability or deployed investment.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned that higher advanced-economy yields, energy inflation and AI competition for capital could reverse recent improvements in poorer countries' debt sustainability. She nevertheless described markets as orderly and singled out Senegal as a test of faster G20 Common Framework processing.

## Record supply meets issuer-specific constraints

Dealers expect about $215 billion of US investment-grade issuance in September, above last year's $207.5 billion monthly record, with forecasts ranging from $190 billion to $250 billion. Four of this year's first eight months set monthly records, including the latest three. Yields above 5.5% have not shut the market: spreads remained below 80 basis points for much of the week, encouraging borrowers to advance 2027 funding.

Repeated AI deals also raise concentration questions. Many IG mandates cap single-company exposure at 3%–5%. The largest technology borrowers may remain below those limits, but an expanding calendar gives investors more alternatives for each additional commitment.

ByteDance secured a $29.6 billion dollar loan, up from its initial $20 billion target after strong bank commitments. Asia's second-largest dollar borrowing of 2026 will support accelerated AI investment. Public Storage is meanwhile discussing its first Canadian-dollar sale, about C$500 million for seven years at initial guidance near 95 basis points over government debt. It follows a C$1.2 billion acquisition of 68 facilities; US senior unsecured ratings are A2/A.

AirAsia says up to $1 billion of international debt and RM700 million of local facilities would refinance costly pandemic obligations, not fund operating losses. It placed a $230 million route-revenue-backed private-credit bond in April and borrowed $443 million in 2024 from funds including Ares at coupons up to 11%. Unhedged fuel costs and limited fare pass-through contributed to a RM527 million quarterly loss, the largest in four years. Shares have fallen 64% since the Iran war began, complicating a refinancing intended to reduce interest costs.

Cerba Healthcare requested French conciliation proceedings for about €5 billion of debt. The EQT-backed laboratory company's net debt exceeded €4.9 billion, or nine times trailing earnings, against June cash of €108 million. A €100 million sponsor loan supports liquidity, and lenders extended an interest grace period to November. Second-quarter EBITDA rose about 12% to over €122 million and revenue 2% to €469 million, insufficient to repair leverage amid uncertainty over French reimbursement tariffs.

CSN bonds instead rose after Benjamin Steinbruch stepped down immediately as CEO after more than two decades, becoming chairman, and former Vale chief Fabio Schvartsman took the operating role. CSN seeks about $2.9 billion from cement and infrastructure stake sales. Its 11% 2030 bonds gained 2.25 cents to 80.5 and shares as much as 20%, reflecting greater confidence in execution before any completed deleveraging.

New York's MTA disclosed a $785 million issue backed by taxes on property sales of at least $2 million. Expected receipts of nearly $400 million this year and roughly $350 million annually in 2027–30 compare with about $150 million of annual debt service after issuance. Moody's rates the structure A1 and S&P recently upgraded it to AA-. The sale exhausts the statutory annual principal-and-interest cap for these securities; the dedicated tax pledge, rather than broad transit operations, underpins repayment.

Chicago's corporate-fund outlook is less comfortable. Mayor Brandon Johnson forecasts an $882 million deficit in 2027 as bond payments, cost-of-living adjustments, commodity inflation and reduced tax-increment-financing surpluses raise pressure. This year's budget retains an $85 million gap after revenue measures, including a proposed debt-collections sale, disappointed. A $364 million supplemental pension payment is planned next year. Refinancing savings and leftover pandemic reserves address the nearer shortfall, not the recurring 2027 imbalance.

China's rating reforms could produce more issuer differentiation. Nearly 90% of over 6,500 domestic credit-bond issuers are AA or higher, versus 4.4% in the US. S&P noted that a globally B-rated borrower could receive AAA treatment on a panda bond, citing a 15.34% five-year cumulative potential default rate for the global B category. PBOC pressure since April to reduce top-rating concentration has prompted downgrades and withdrawals across the CN¥37 trillion market.

## Payrolls come first, followed by inflation and heavy issuance

September 4 payrolls, due at 8:30 a.m. ET, are expected to rise 56,000 after a 23,000 decline, with unemployment at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% after 0.1%. Soft hiring and wages would support Waller's willingness to wait; stronger employment or pay would reinforce the demand signal from services.

The price evidence he emphasized follows next week. September 10 headline and core PPI are each forecast to rise 0.3% month over month, with August CPI on September 11. Treasury 3-, 10- and 30-year auctions and renewed corporate supply will compete for demand before the inflation outlook is settled. Even if payrolls soften, sticky non-energy prices or weak bidding could limit long-end gains.

The ECB meets September 10 with a 25-basis-point increase to 2.50% widely expected. Guidance beyond that move will distinguish the economists' one-and-done forecast from market pricing. The BOJ's September 18 quarter-point increase is nearly fully discounted, putting more weight on its subsequent pace. Delay or guidance ruling out further hikes would undermine the policy support for the yen's rally and could renew intervention concerns.

section_summaries.section_title: Waller opens the door to a Fed hold, lifting Treasuries
section_summaries.summary: Waller reduced the urgency of a September hike. Front-end yields fell most, while stronger services and expensive oil left inflation risks unresolved.

section_summaries.section_title: Strong service orders leave Waller waiting for inflation, not recession
section_summaries.summary: Service orders and technology imports showed demand strength alongside subdued hiring. Waller's willingness to wait coexisted with a higher neutral-rate estimate and fiscal concerns.

section_summaries.section_title: BOJ signals, rather than another intervention, sustain the yen rally
section_summaries.summary: BOJ signals and positioning supported the yen; account data did not suggest another large intervention. Auction demand improved on average, while GPIF and hedge adjustments remain prospective.

section_summaries.section_title: Europe's energy shortage keeps the next hike in view
section_summaries.summary: Europe's gas gap strengthened the immediate hike case without settling the endpoint. Malaysia sounded less comfortable, while Turkey, Poland and Hungary faced different inflation and fiscal constraints.

section_summaries.section_title: Pakistan raises record dollars; India weighs how to absorb its surplus
section_summaries.summary: Pakistan replaced some short-term dependence with term debt. India considered sterilizing surplus rupees, the Philippines reassessed supply, and Venezuela's bond rally preceded agreed recovery terms.

ByteDance enlarged completed funding as Cerba sought conciliation. AirAsia's operating losses, CSN's asset-sale execution and contrasting municipal revenue structures mattered more than flat average spreads.

section_summaries.section_title: Payrolls come first, followed by inflation and heavy issuance
section_summaries.summary: Payrolls first test Fed patience. Inflation releases, Treasury auctions and renewed corporate supply follow, alongside ECB and BOJ guidance on how far tightening extends.

overall_summary.headline: Waller's hold option rallies Treasuries despite stronger services
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Waller said further inflation progress could justify leaving rates unchanged, without ruling out a hike if prices accelerated. ISM services rose to 55.4, with stronger orders but employment still contracting. Real yields fell while breakevens edged higher.

The yen gained 2% as BOJ reports favored a quarter-point increase and flexible follow-through. Account data argued against another large intervention. Japan's 30-year auction drew above-average coverage, though a wider tail showed buyers still sought a concession.

Pakistan completed a record $3 billion bond sale and ByteDance secured a larger $29.6 billion loan. Cerba sought court-supervised talks, while record September supply and issuer concentration kept credit selection important despite stable US spreads.
overall_summary.summary: The 2-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.34%, while the 10- and 30-year declined 2 to 4.77% and 5.25%. September hike odds retreated toward 50%, but service orders and prices accelerated.
